summary: This informational RFC presents use cases that share a common need: encoding network action indicators and associated ancillary data inside MPLS packets. There is community interest in extending the MPLS data plane to carry such information, and these use cases motivate that work.

eli5.summary: Some delivery jobs need a note stuck on each parcel saying what special handling to do. This lists the real situations where that would help.

questions: why put ancillary data in mpls packets
why carry ancillary data in mpls packets
subtitle: Why MPLS networks want a way to mark packets with actions and carry extra data alongside them.

tldr.problem: Several MPLS features need special handling by forwarding hardware, but the existing tools, Special-Purpose Labels and Extended Special-Purpose Labels, are either very scarce or cost an extra label stack entry per action.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC does not define a protocol. It lists use cases (no further fast reroute, hybrid measurement, network slicing, service function chaining, network programming) that would all benefit from MPLS Network Actions: indicators that an action is needed, plus ancillary data.
tldr.outcome: The use cases motivate the MNA framework in RFC 9789 and are not an exhaustive set. Solutions are left to future documents.

today: RFC 9791 is an Informational document that has not been obsoleted or updated. It is a companion to the MNA framework in RFC 9789, and the use cases are described as not exhaustive.

sections.title: Why MPLS Needs Network Actions
sections.content:
This document describes use cases that introduce functions requiring special processing by forwarding hardware. Today that means allocating a new Special-Purpose Label (SPL, from RFC 3032) or an Extended Special-Purpose Label (eSPL). SPLs are a very limited resource, and an eSPL needs an extra label stack entry for every network action, which is expensive.

The MPLS Network Action (MNA) approach, requirements for which are in RFC 9613, was proposed to extend the MPLS architecture. MNA is expected to enable functions that carry additional ancillary data in the packet, plus a way to say that the data is present and that a specific action must be performed.

Ancillary data is either in-stack data, which sits inside the MPLS label stack, or post-stack data, which sits after the Bottom of Stack (BoS). The use cases here feed the general MNA framework of RFC 9789.
sections.eli5: Special stickers on parcels are scarce, and each extra sticker makes the parcel bulkier. MNA is a better way to say 'do something special' and attach a small note.

sections.title: Fast Reroute and Measurement
sections.content:
No further Fast Reroute. MPLS Fast Reroute (FRR) minimises packet loss when a link or node fails. If a packet that was already rerouted meets a second failure at another node, it may loop between the Label Switching Routers that activated FRR until its TTL expires, causing congestion and loss. The proposal is to mark packets that FRR has redirected using MNA, so that no further FRR processing is applied.

Hybrid measurement. MNA can carry the information needed to measure the experience of the marked packet, and can optionally carry telemetry collected on a router. Two examples are given. In situ OAM (IOAM, RFC 9197 and RFC 9326) runs in Ingress to Egress or Hop by Hop mode and has Option-Types such as Pre-allocated Trace, Incremental Trace, Edge-to-Edge, Proof-of-Transit and Direct Export (DEX). With every type except DEX the data travels in the trigger packet; with DEX the data is exported according to local policy.

The Alternate Marking Method (RFC 9341, RFC 9342) measures packet loss and delay, and MNA is an alternative way to support it in MPLS to the Synonymous Flow Label framework of RFC 8957.
sections.eli5: If a parcel has already taken a detour once, a sticker tells the next worker not to send it on another detour. Other stickers let the sorting centre time how long a parcel takes.

sections.title: Slicing, Service Chaining and Network Programming
sections.content:
Network slicing. A network slice service provides connectivity coupled with network resource commitments. Packets associated with a Network Resource Partition (NRP) may carry a marking called the NRP Selector, which maps the packet to its resources and forwarding treatment. Routers on a link shared by several NRPs must identify the NRP of each packet, and MNA can carry the NRP Selector in MPLS packets.

NSH-based service function chaining. RFC 8595 emulates the Network Service Header using only MPLS label stack entries, which has limitations. MNA could extend this emulation to support the NSH Context Headers, for example a Flow ID (RFC 9263) used for load-balancing among Service Function Forwarders.

Network programming. In Segment Routing an ingress node steers a packet through an ordered list of segments, each a function at a specific place in the network. It may be desirable to encode a pointer to a function and its arguments in an MPLS packet, and MNA can encode the FUNC::ARGs, the functional equivalent of what RFC 8986 does in Segment Routing over IPv6.
sections.eli5: Stickers could also say which delivery lane a parcel belongs to, which checkpoints it must visit, or give small instructions to run at certain stops.

sections.title: Coexistence With Existing Services
sections.content:
MPLS already carries Layer 3 and Layer 2 services, and data after the BoS can look like several things. The first nibble (four bits) of the data right after the BoS is 0b0000 when a pseudowire Control Word is present, 0b0001 for a Generic Associated Channel carrying OAM data, and 0b0101 for BIER traffic encapsulated over MPLS.

MPLS can also be the data plane for Deterministic Networking (DetNet), which uses the label stack, the DetNet control word and the DetNet Associated Channel Header. MNA solutions for these and future use cases are expected to coexist with, and stay backward compatible with, all existing MPLS services.

Several use cases may also be needed in the same packet, which then carries multiple pieces of in-stack or post-stack ancillary data. For example, IOAM can collect performance data on a network slice flow to help check that the slice's Service Level Objectives are met.
sections.eli5: New stickers must not confuse workers who already know the old ones, and one parcel may need several stickers at once.

sections.title: Use Cases Still Under Discussion
sections.content:
Appendix A lists aspirational cases whose discussion was ongoing at publication. Generic Delivery Functions would place headers, such as a Generic Fragmentation Header, in the post-stack data block, possibly as a list of headers. Delay budgets for time-bound applications ask for packets to reach their destination within a time budget; Segment Routing can pick a short path but does not influence queueing at each router.

A stack-based latency method would insert a stack of local deadlines, one per router, with the Top of Stack deadline for the first router and the BoS for the last. Only the ingress router needs to know the flow requirements, so admitting a new flow means updating only its information base.
sections.eli5: A few more ideas are still being talked about, like writing a deadline for each stop on the parcel.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC points to Section 7 of RFC 9789, which covers documents that do not specify protocols, and the authors state that these considerations fully apply. A detailed security analysis of each use case is out of scope and is left to future solution documents, which are strongly recommended to get security review early, ideally during Working Group Last Call. The document has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: This list does not build anything yet, so the safety checks are left for when real stickers are designed.

viz.caption: THE USE CASES IN THE MAIN BODY

items.title: No further FRR
items.text: Mark rerouted packets so a second failure does not trigger another reroute.

items.title: Hybrid measurement
items.text: Carry IOAM or Alternate Marking data to measure loss and delay.

items.title: Network slicing
items.text: Carry the NRP Selector so routers apply the right treatment.

items.title: Service chaining
items.text: Extend NSH emulation with context headers such as a Flow ID.

items.title: Network programming
items.text: Encode a function and its arguments, like FUNC::ARG in SRv6.

viz.caption: FIRST NIBBLE AFTER THE BOTTOM OF STACK

items.label: PW Control Word
items.desc: Pseudowire control word follows the MPLS header.

items.label: Associated channel
items.desc: Control channel for a PW, LSP or section, for OAM data.
